learning_objectives: Explain energy requirements and ATP transfer.
Compare respiratory substrates and calculate RQ.

sections.heading: Cellular energy
sections.body: Energy is needed for active transport against gradients, movement including muscle contraction, and anabolic reactions such as DNA replication and protein synthesis.

sections.heading: ATP
sections.body: ATP is a nucleotide containing adenine, ribose and three phosphate groups. Hydrolysis of the terminal phosphate transfers energy. ATP is small, soluble, mobile and rapidly regenerated. Substrate-linked phosphorylation transfers phosphate directly from a substrate to ADP; chemiosmosis uses proton flow through ATP synthase in mitochondrial and chloroplast membranes.

sections.heading: Respiratory substrates
sections.body: Approximate energy values: carbohydrate 17 kJ g-1, protein 17 kJ g-1, lipid 39 kJ g-1. Lipids are more reduced and contain more C-H bonds per gram, so oxidation releases more energy.

sections.heading: RQ
sections.body: RQ = CO2 produced / O2 consumed. Glucose oxidation gives 6/6 = 1.00. Palmitic acid oxidation gives 32/45 = 0.71. Typical lipid RQ is about 0.7; protein varies.

sections.heading: Respirometer practical
sections.body: A sealed respirometer containing separated soda lime or KOH absorbs CO2. The fall in gas volume or pressure indicates O2 uptake. A non-respiring bead control corrects for temperature and pressure. This alone does not determine RQ: CO2 production must also be measured over the same interval using a paired/differential or validated separate method. Control mass, temperature, time and apparatus volume; repeat and calculate a mean.

questions.question: Define RQ.
questions.answer: The ratio of CO2 produced to O2 consumed during respiration.

questions.question: A sample consumes 4.0 cm3 O2 and produces 2.8 cm3 CO2. Calculate RQ.
Why does a CO2-absorbing respirometer not measure RQ by itself?
questions.answer: It measures O2 uptake while CO2 is absorbed. RQ also requires CO2 production.

questions.question: Explain why ATP is suitable for immediate energy transfer rather than long-term energy storage.
questions.answer: ATP is soluble and mobile, releases energy in manageable amounts by hydrolysis and can be rapidly regenerated. Carbohydrates and lipids are better suited to longer-term energy storage.

questions.question: State the approximate energy values per gram of carbohydrate, protein and lipid.
questions.answer: Carbohydrate about 17 kJ g−1, protein about 17 kJ g−1 and lipid about 39 kJ g−1.

questions.question: Explain why protein is not usually the preferred respiratory substrate.
questions.answer: Proteins have essential structural and functional roles, and amino groups must be removed before their carbon skeletons can be used in respiration.

questions.question: A respiratory equation produces 18 molecules of CO2 and uses 24 molecules of O2. Calculate RQ.
Give one reason why an RQ value may not identify a single respiratory substrate with certainty.
questions.answer: An organism may respire a mixture of substrates, giving an intermediate RQ.

questions.question: Describe one way to measure carbon dioxide production separately from oxygen uptake in an RQ investigation.
questions.answer: Use a paired or differential respirometer arrangement, or a validated separate CO2 measurement, so CO2 output and O2 uptake are measured over the same interval.

questions.question: Why should the mass and developmental stage of germinating seeds be standardised?
questions.answer: Respiration rate varies with organism mass and developmental/activity state; standardising these makes comparisons fair.

questions.question: Identify two sources of error in a simple respirometer investigation.
questions.answer: Possible errors include gas leaks, temperature changes, pressure changes, organism movement and inconsistent reading of capillary position.

questions.question: Why must the respirometer be airtight?
questions.answer: Gas entering or leaving through leaks changes the measured gas volume independently of respiration, making oxygen uptake inaccurate.

questions.question: Explain why a lipid respiratory substrate commonly has a lower RQ than carbohydrate.
questions.answer: Lipid oxidation consumes proportionally more oxygen relative to carbon dioxide produced, giving a lower CO2/O2 ratio.
mark_points: More O2 used relative to CO2

questions.question: State one limitation of using capillary movement as an estimate of respiration rate.
questions.answer: Movement can be affected by temperature or atmospheric pressure changes, leaks or movement of the organism, so controls and equilibration are needed.
